claim: An Arduino Uno-based MPPT solar charge controller using the Perturb & Observe algorithm, an LM7815 regulator, and 2SC5200 current-boost transistors can manage up to 60A and charge a 12V lead-acid battery from a 50W-600W solar panel.
stance_target: feasibility of low-cost Arduino-based MPPT charge controller as a B.Tech ECE project
scope_conditions: off-grid/high-current solar charging application, 2024 paper, Nigeria-based authors
quoted_support: The technology can manage a maximum current of 60A and charge a battery bank effectively... This design can be used to charge a standard 12V lead acid battery with a 50W to 600W solar panel.

claim: Prior research (Hussein et al. 1995) found MPPT increases PV power-extraction efficiency to about 97% compared to non-MPPT systems.
stance_target: value of MPPT over fixed-point solar charging
scope_conditions: PV solar systems, comparative study cited within 2024 paper
quoted_support: It clearly shows that when we use MPPT with the PV system, the power extraction efficiency is increase to 97%.

claim: The Perturb & Observe (hill-climbing) algorithm is the most widely used MPPT method in practice due to its simplicity of implementation.
stance_target: choice of MPPT algorithm for student solar charge controller projects
scope_conditions: MPPT algorithm selection for PV charge controllers
quoted_support: Perturb & observe (P&O) algorithm's simplicity and ease to implement, is sometimes referred to as the "hill climbing" method and is the most widely used algorithm in practice.
